front: Default Cisco IOS OSPF administrative distance?
back: 110. It is separate from the OSPF cost.

front: OSPFv2 protocol number and multicast groups?
back: IP protocol 89; 224.0.0.5 AllSPFRouters, 224.0.0.6 AllDRouters. No TCP/UDP port.

front: How do DBD and LSU packets differ?
back: A DBD summarizes database contents. An LSU carries the actual link-state advertisements being distributed.

front: How does IOS choose a RID when a process starts?
back: Explicit router-id; otherwise highest eligible up IPv4 loopback, then highest eligible active IPv4 interface. Verify the active RID.

front: Normal IOS Hello/dead defaults for broadcast and point-to-point?
back: 10/40 seconds. An explicitly configured dead interval can differ; compare effective values on both ends.

front: What do 2-Way and Full establish?
back: 2-Way confirms bidirectional Hello recognition. Full means database synchronization completed for that adjacency.

front: Which two timer values must agree on the intended OSPF neighbor link?
back: The effective Hello and dead intervals. Compare interface output on both ends; do not infer the effective values from one command alone.

front: Repeated ExStart/Exchange: which common fault should you check?
back: Compare interface MTUs and exchange errors. MTU mismatch is common, not the only cause; correct the mismatch before considering a bypass.

front: When is 2WAY/DROTHER normal?
back: Between two DROTHERs on a broadcast segment, while each is Full with the DR and BDR.

front: What breaks a fresh DR election tie in interface priority?
back: The higher router ID, among eligible routers. Existing DR/BDR roles require separate non-preemption reasoning.

front: Broadcast versus point-to-point OSPF roles?
back: Broadcast elects DR/BDR. Point-to-point has no DR/BDR and normally shows FULL/ -.

front: Configure OSPF point-to-point on a two-router Ethernet link?
back: ip ospf network point-to-point under both interfaces. Ethernet framing stays Ethernet.

front: IOS automatic OSPF cost formula and default reference?
back: Reference bandwidth / configured interface bandwidth, integer cost with minimum 1. Default reference 100 Mbps.

front: Why can Fast Ethernet and Gigabit Ethernet both have automatic OSPF cost 1?
back: With the default 100-Mbps reference, the computed integer cost has a minimum of 1. A higher consistent reference can distinguish faster links.

front: Which interface costs make up a route metric?
back: Outgoing costs from the calculating router to the destination, including the remote LAN interface; do not add receiving costs again.

front: Set an OSPF reference of 1 Gbps?
back: auto-cost reference-bandwidth 1000 in router mode, consistently across the routing domain. Units are Mbps.

front: Two IOS ways to enable OSPFv2 on an interface?
back: A matching network ADDRESS WILDCARD area statement, or ip ospf PROCESS area AREA directly on the interface.

front: What does a passive OSPF interface still advertise?
back: Its enabled, up connected prefix, through other OSPF links. It does not form neighbors on that interface.

front: Must neighboring routers use the same OSPF process number?
back: No. The process number is a local configuration label; the area must agree and router IDs must be unique.

front: What does [110/11] in an IOS OSPF route mean?
back: Administrative distance 110, total OSPF cost 11. Neither number is the prefix length.

front: Does OSPF priority 0 disable adjacency formation?
back: No. It prevents DR/BDR election eligibility; the router can still form Full adjacencies with the elected routers.

front: A higher-priority OSPF router joins a healthy broadcast segment: must it become DR?
back: No. Existing DR/BDR roles are non-preemptive.

front: Which wins: automatic OSPF cost or explicit ip ospf cost?
back: The explicit interface cost overrides the automatic bandwidth calculation.

front: Does a host wildcard in an OSPF network command advertise a /32?
back: No. It selects the interface by address. An ordinary Ethernet LAN is advertised using its actual interface prefix.

front: Does Full prove that every intended client LAN is advertised?
back: No. Verify the remote LAN interface state, activation and its route separately.

front: Can R1 and R3 calculate different costs over the same physical link?
back: Yes. Each uses its own outgoing interface cost; reverse-direction configuration need not be equal.
